newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India steadies after slide.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India steadies after slide.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts steadied on Tuesday after a sharp slide in prices this week induced by Finance Minister P Chidambaram's refusal to lessen the impact of new corporate taxes.
"It had to come to an end, there were a few people out on the bid there," said a trader.

The James Capel Indian GDR Index rose 0.56 points, or 0.81 percent, to 69.85 points, a premium of 12.99 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index rose 8.83 points to 3,391.54.
Indian Hotels and East India Hotels both turned higher, with the former adding 63 cents to $25.25/$26.25 and East India 75 cents to $20.00/$21.00, while Bajaj put on 75 cents to $34.35/$35.35.

The Capel Korea Index fell 0.62 points, 0.91 percent, to 67.15 points, apremium of 22.56 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index shed 3.84 points to provisionally close at 797.61.

The Capel Taiwan Index fell 1.1 points, 1.23 percent, to 89.07 points, a premium of 3.56 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index ended down 29.76 points or 0.46 percent at 6,425.68, down from an opening high of 6,476.71.
